Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
311 PM EDT Thu Oct 1 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 310 PM EDT Thursday...

The wind gust potential for tonight has increased, though just how 
strong gusts will be is still somewhat uncertain.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 310 PM EDT Thursday...

1. A cold front will bring widespread showers and gusty winds 
to the region tonight and Friday, with falling temperatures Friday 
afternoon. 

2. Beautiful fall weather expected for the weekend. 

3. Showers Sunday night into Monday and colder temperatures 
early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 310 PM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Mostly cloudy skies will prevail through much of the 
rest of the afternoon and evening hours today. While a few showers 
can't be ruled out, especially across northern New York, much of the 
area will remain dry until tonight, when more widespread rain 
associated with a cold front will pass through. Moisture will 
increase this evening and overnight on a strong SW jet, approaching 
60 kt at 850 mb. This will make for very windy conditions on the 
summits overnight, where gusts of 50+ mph are expected. The question 
is how much of this jet is able to make it down to lower elevations, 
especially since the core of the jet will somewhat aligned with the 
area of heavier showers. Guidance is somewhat split on this; the 
NAM3 is the most generous with mixing, especially along the favored 
northern/eastern slopes of the Adirondacks and Greens, with gusts of 
30-40 mph overnight. The HRRR keeps things more stable and limits 
gusts to mainly under 30 mph below 2500 ft, while the RRFS is 
somewhere in the middle. HREF probabilities of gusts greater than 30 
mph are 65-85% in the higher terrain and in those favored eastern 
slope areas, but feel this is somewhat skewed by the NAM3 which is 
probably overdone. Have increased gusts with this package, but have 
stayed closer to the 30 mph limit advertised by the HRRR. Still, 
wouldn't be surprised to see some higher gusts in the aforementioned 
favored areas. And, of course, expect locally higher gusts on Lake 
Champlain; more on that in the Marine section below. 

As mentioned, moisture increases overnight ahead of the front, with 
PWATs 1.50-1.75 inches. As such, anticipate rain will be moderate to 
perhaps briefly heavy at times. However, the front will be making 
fairly decent forward progress, so expect the main swath of showers 
will be transient enough to preclude any flooding threat. Rain moves 
into the St Lawrence Valley around midnight or so, then pushes 
southeast overnight, stretching from the Northeast Kingdom through 
the Champlain Valley and down into the High Peaks region by daybreak 
Friday. The showers will diminish a bit in intensity and coverage as 
the band moves into central and southern VT. A secondary front will 
follow the main cold front and the main band of rain, ushering in a 
much drier airmass. Can't rule out a few lingering showers late in 
the day, but overall the bulk of the rain will be done by 4 or 5 pm. 
Temperatures tonight will remain fairly steady given the cloud 
cover, increasing moisture, and south/southwest winds, but expect 
they will fall fairly sharply on Friday as the rain spreads into the 
area and the cold front moves through. As such, highs on Friday will 
be coolest in northern NY and the Northeast Kingdom where highs will 
only be in the low/mid 60s, while southern VT will likely see 70s 
before the rain arrives.

KEY MESSAGE 2: High pressure will settle across the region Saturday, 
then begin to shift eastward on Sunday. The result will be crisp, 
fall-like weather with plenty of sunshine, especially on Saturday. 
Highs on Saturday will be in the mid 50s to mid 60s with north winds 
5-10 mph. High pressure crests directly overhead Saturday night, so 
expect a chilly night with lows in the mid 20s to mid 30s, except 
close to 40F near Lake Champlain. Winds turn to the south on Sunday 
as the ridge axis moves east, which will bring slightly warmer 
temperatures and increasing cloud cover for the second half of the 
weekend. However, no rain is expected during the daylight hours. It 
should be a perfect weekend for leaf peeping, so hope everyone can 
get out and enjoy the foliage!

KEY MESSAGE 3: Our next chance for some showers across the region will 
be Sunday night into Monday as a surface cold front crosses our 
area. Temperatures will range from the 40s at night to 50s during 
the day, therefore only rain showers anticipated for this timeframe. 
Drier and cooler weather will return for much of the rest of the 
week as a ridge of surface high pressure builds into our area from 
Canada. Monday night and Tuesday night will both be quite cold with 
temperatures well below freezing in the coldest hollows of the Dacks 
and Northeast Kingdom. All other locations will be below freezing as 
well, except closest to Lake Champlain where it will remain a bit 
warmer due to the warm lake water. The coldest daytime period of the 
week will be on Tuesday as highs top out in the mid 40s to lower 
50s. Temperatures will moderate from Wednesday onward.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 18Z Friday...Clouds remain in place across the region.
MVFR ceilings are present at MSS, RUT and SLK. Other sites are
all VFR bust still OVC. Winds have become more southwesterly in
some spots with wind speeds 7 to 13 knots sustained with gusts 
16 to 22 knots. As winds start subsiding around 20-21z, LLWS 
will be possible, mainly over KMSS and KSLK then spread east 
beyond 00z Friday. Additionally, some isolated rain showers may 
reach Adirondacks in the 18-20z timeframe. Main shower 
activity with potential MVFR conditions enter KMSS around 00z 
with KSLK around 04z and after 06z Fri east. Mainly MVFR
conditions are anticipated with lowered visibilities and
ceilings in showers. 

Outlook...

Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory is in effect for the rest of today through
tonight. South winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts to 30 kt are
expected. Waves generally 1 to 3 feet, locally up to 4 feet. 

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
